related_questions.question: Do I need a visa to visit Greece?

text_blocks.snippet: No, if you are a US citizen with a valid US passport, you do not need a visa to visit Greece for tourism purposes for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period. You can enter Greece visa-free for tourism, business, or transit purposes. However, you will need to comply with the Schengen Area's 90/180-day rule.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, if you are a US citizen with a valid US passport, you do not need a visa to visit Greece for tourism purposes for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period

list.title: Visa-free travel:
list.snippet: Greece is part of the Schengen Area, which allows citizens of certain countries, including the US, to enter without a visa for short stays.

list.title: 90/180-day rule:
list.snippet: You can stay in Greece (and other Schengen countries) for a maximum of 90 days within a 180-day period without needing a visa.

list.title: Passport validity:
list.snippet: Your passport should be valid for at least three months beyond your intended departure date from Greece and have at least two blank pages.

list.title: Other requirements:
list.snippet: You may be asked to provide documentation proving the purpose of your visit and your departure date.

list.title: Official and diplomatic passports:
list.snippet: If you are traveling on an official or diplomatic passport, you will need a Schengen visa even for short stays.

list.title: Applying for a visa:
list.snippet: If you need a visa for a longer stay or for other purposes, you can apply for a short-term "Schengen visa" or a long-term "national visa". You can find information about visa applications on the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs website.

related_questions.question: Can I live in Greece as a US citizen?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, US citizens can live in Greece, but they will need to obtain the appropriate visa and residency permit for stays longer than 90 days. For short stays (up to 90 days within a 180-day period), US citizens can enter Greece for tourism, business, or family visits without a visa.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, US citizens can live in Greece, but they will need to obtain the appropriate visa and residency permit for stays longer than 90 days

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of how to live in Greece as a US citizen:

list.snippet: No visa is required for stays up to 90 days within a 180-day period.
Passport must be valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay.
Proof of sufficient funds for the stay and a return ticket are required.
Travel insurance is highly recommended according to Immigrant Invest.

list.title: Residency Permit:
list.snippet: US citizens need a residency permit for stays longer than 90 days, unless they also hold an EU or EEA passport.

list.title: National D Visa:
list.snippet: Before applying for a residency permit, a national D visa is usually required to enter Greece.

list.title: Purpose of Stay:
list.snippet: Residency permits can be obtained for various reasons, such as work, study, or family reunification.

list.title: Special Programs:
list.snippet: There are also specific programs for retirees, digital nomads, and investors (Golden Visa).

Retirement: The Financially Independent Person (FIP) scheme, also known as the Greek retirement visa, is a common option. It requires proof of a stable monthly income of at least €2,000 (approx. $2,150) or savings of €24,000-€84,000 (approx. $25,800-$90,300) in a Greek bank account, along with full-coverage medical insurance from a Greek provider.
Digital Nomads: There are specific visa options for digital nomads.
Golden Visa: This program allows non-EU citizens to obtain residency by investing in Greece, often in real estate (minimum investment of €250,000 or $278,000).
Family Reunification: US citizens married to EU or Greek citizens may also have residency options.
Study: Students can apply for a visa to study in Greece.
Employment: A US citizen can be sponsored by a Greek employer according to Lynn Roulo.
Valid passport.
Proof of sufficient funds according to Immigrant Invest.
Proof of address in Greece.
Health insurance.
Potentially, a clean criminal record and other documents depending on the specific visa type.
Apply for the appropriate visa from a Greek consulate in the US .
Enter Greece with the visa .
Apply for a residence permit at the local municipality office or Decentralized Administration office .
Obtain a temporary residence permit, which can be renewed .
After five years, you may be eligible for a permanent residence permit .
The application process for residency permits can be complex, and it is recommended to seek legal advice or assistance from an immigration expert.
While some sources suggest that the application process can take 3-6 months according to Get Golden Visa, this can vary.
It's crucial to understand the specific requirements for the visa or program you are applying for and to ensure you meet all eligibility criteria.

related_questions.snippet: U.S. citizens are generally allowed to travel to Greece without a visa if they are coming for tourism for a short time. However, the decision on admission to Greece is made by Greek immigration authorities in accordance with Greek law.

text_blocks.snippet: To visit Greece, you may need a visa depending on your nationality and the purpose and duration of your stay. U.S. citizens generally don't need a visa for stays under 90 days for tourism or business, but they do need one for longer stays or if they are holders of U.S. diplomatic or official passports. For stays longer than 90 days, or if you are a U.S. citizen holding a diplomatic or official passport, you'll need to apply for a visa at the Greek Consulate or Embassy.
snippet_highlighted_words: U.S. citizens generally don't need a visa for stays under 90 days for tourism or business, but they do need one for longer stays or if they are holders of U.S. diplomatic or official passports

list.title: Schengen Visa (Short-term):
list.snippet: For stays up to 90 days, you might need a Schengen visa if your nationality requires it, according to VisaHQ. Check the specific requirements based on your nationality.

list.title: National Visa (Long-term):
list.snippet: If you plan to stay in Greece for longer than 90 days, you'll need a National visa, also known as a Type D visa, which allows for stays up to 365 days.

list.title: U.S. Citizens:
list.snippet: Generally, U.S. citizens don't need a visa for short stays up to 90 days for tourism or business. However, they need a visa for longer stays or if they hold a diplomatic or official passport.

list.title: Application Process:
list.snippet: Applications for both Schengen and National visas need to be submitted in person, often by appointment, at the Greek Consulate or Embassy with jurisdiction over your place of residence.

list.title: Supporting Documents:
list.snippet: Common documents include a valid passport, proof of travel insurance, proof of accommodation (hotel reservation or invitation), round-trip tickets, and financial means to support your stay.

list.title: Processing Time:
list.snippet: Schengen visa processing can take around 15 days, but may be extended to 30 or even 60 days in some cases, according to VisaHQ. National visa processing times can vary.

list.title: Contacting the Consulate:
list.snippet: For specific questions about visa requirements or to schedule an appointment, contact the Greek Consulate or Embassy in your area.
